problem.statement_latex: A classical verifier interacts with an untrusted device and outputs $Z$ with conditional smooth min-entropy $H_{\min}^{\varepsilon}(Z\mid E,\mathrm{transcript})\geq k$, for the side information $E$ admitted by the protocol. A seeded extractor gives nearly uniform bits. Complexity counts prover gates, communication, verification, and certified entropy.

evidence.description_latex: LWE-based certification has a cryptographic proof; the circuit experiment has a security analysis for its restricted adversary.

hardware.description_latex: The circuit protocol was demonstrated on 56 trapped-ion qubits; trapdoor-function protocols require coherent cryptographic circuits.

quantum.headline_latex: BCMVV uses polynomially many cryptographic rounds to certify entropy under LWE-based assumptions. A separate random-circuit protocol executes challenged circuits and classically checks selected probabilities. Its 2025 experiment certified $71{,}313$ entropy bits with 56 trapped-ion qubits under a restricted-adversary model.
quantum.headline_text: BCMVV uses polynomially many cryptographic rounds to certify entropy under LWE-based assumptions. A separate random-circuit protocol executes challenged circuits and classically checks selected probabilities. Its 2025 experiment certified $71{,}313$ entropy bits with 56 trapped-ion qubits under a restricted-adversary model.

classical.headline_latex: A classical device can retain every output, yielding zero conditional entropy against its own side information. The circuit-based protocol bounds the number of samples obtainable by a time-limited classical adversary; its verification used combined sustained performance $1.1\times10^{18}$ floating-point operations per second.
